title: Map required analysis dimensions to rubric before cleaning data
when_to_use: When the task or rubric specifies required grouping dimensions, bins, or metrics for analysis.
experience:
- At the start, extract all required analysis dimensions, bins, and metrics from the rubric or task description.
- Create a mapping table linking each required dimension (e.g., binned Age, binned Mileage, Color, Electric Range) to the corresponding data column(s) and required transformation.
- Validate data availability and structure for each required dimension before proceeding with cleaning or analysis.
- Ensure your cleaning and transformation pipeline explicitly produces all required dimensions (e.g., create binned columns, standardize categorical values).
- After cleaning, verify that your dataset contains all dimensions needed for the full analysis scope specified in the rubric.
checklist: Transform/create all required dimensions in cleaning
Verify final dataset includes all rubric-required fields
common_failure_prevented: Failing to analyze required dimensions (like binned age, color, electric range) because they were not created during data cleaning, leading to incomplete grouping analysis.

title: Build multivariate model before reporting single-factor correlations
when_to_use: When the task asks to analyze which factors influence an outcome or compare configurations.
experience:
- Before reporting single-factor trends or correlations, explicitly design a multivariate model (e.g., linear regression) that includes all potential influencing factors.
- Prepare the data by encoding categorical variables, handling missing values, and scaling if necessary for the model.
- Fit the model and extract standardized coefficients, p-values, and model fit statistics (R²).
- Use the model results to rank factors by their relative contribution to the outcome.
- Report the multivariate model's findings (key drivers, effect sizes, significance) before or alongside any simple descriptive group comparisons.
common_failure_prevented: Reporting only simple correlations (like age vs. outcome) without a multivariate analysis, missing the relative importance of factors and their combined effect.

title: Define and apply a standardized grouping key for model/configuration analysis
when_to_use: When analyzing performance or value by model, series, or configuration across a dataset with free-text descriptions.
experience:
- Before grouping by model or configuration, examine the free-text field (e.g., 'Title') and define a consistent rule or dictionary to extract a standardized grouping key.
- Test the rule on a sample to ensure it correctly aggregates all variations of the same model/configuration.
- Apply the rule to create a new column (e.g., 'Model_Group') in your dataset.
- Validate the grouping by checking the distinct values and counts, ensuring logical consolidation.
- Use this standardized column for all subsequent model-level aggregations and rankings.
common_failure_prevented: Using inconsistent or overly broad grouping (like first two words of a title) that fails to correctly aggregate all records for the same model, leading to inaccurate model-level averages.
